title: Kubernetes inventory (one part of one collection)
description: What a kubernetes_inventory job returns, as the kubernetes_inventory member of a device agent job result (docs/design/kubernetes-inventory.md). The device agent reads the Kubernetes API of the cluster it runs in, with its own service account and read-only verbs, and projects each object onto the fields below. The document is closed at every level: a field this schema does not name is an error. Collect posture, never key material: no member can hold the content of a Secret other than certificates, and no member holds a private key. Every pod, Service and declared port is attributed to the cluster (cluster.id, required in every part), to its namespace and to a workload.

collection_id.description: One id per collection, the same in every part of it.

part.description: A collection is sent as `count` job results, `index` 0 first. Part 0 carries `cluster` in full, `sections`, `collector`, `mesh` and `api_server`; the lists may continue across parts. Nothing is to be marked removed until every part has arrived.

tls_secrets.description: Whether this deployment was set up to read TLS Secrets. Only the cluster's administrators can enable it; no job parameter can.

id.description: The UID of the kube-system namespace: the cluster's stable id. Every row of the collection belongs to this cluster.

ca_certificates.description: The cluster CA bundle (the kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMap).

api_endpoints.description: The API server's own endpoints (the endpoints of the default/kubernetes Service).

traefik.description: Traefik's IngressRoutes, IngressRouteTCPs, TLSOptions and TLSStores. Present only when the job parameters carry traefik: true, and not a class: absent means this agent was not asked for, or does not collect, Traefik. not_installed when neither API group serves IngressRoutes.

sections.description: One answer per class, every class every time; traefik only when the job asked for it.

traefik_ingress_routes.description: Sent only when the job parameters carry traefik: true.

traefik_tls_options.description: Sent only when the job parameters carry traefik: true.

traefik_tls_stores.description: Sent only when the job parameters carry traefik: true.

ip.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address. Pod and Service addresses are not unique between clusters: read them only together with cluster.id.

labels.description: Label keys and values in Kubernetes label syntax (a value is at most 63 characters of letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.').

workload_ref.description: The workload a pod or Service belongs to, in the same namespace as the row that carries it. It names one entry of `workloads`.

kind.description: Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, CronJob, Job, ReplicaSet, Pod (a pod nothing owns), Node (a static pod), or the kind of another controller that owns the pods.

condition.description: A Ready-style condition. `message` is the controller's text after redaction, cut to 512 characters.

section.description: How one class answered. ok: read in full, so an empty list means none exist. failed: it should have been readable and was not (rows already read are still sent, and nothing may be marked removed). unsupported: this cluster does not have it, this deployment was not given it, or this release does not collect it.

certificate.description: One certificate, in the field names of defs/certificate.json (a closed subset of it). Each distinct certificate appears once per collection; every other row names it by fingerprint_sha256.

certificate_pem.description: Exactly one CERTIFICATE block. Left out when the job asked for no PEM.

csr.description: What a certificate signing request asks for. The request itself is public; it is parsed and not forwarded.

handshake.description: One TLS handshake the device agent made itself. It makes them only to the API server and to kubelets; every other endpoint is the sensor's to scan.

certificate_chain.description: The chain as served, leaf first.

chains_to_cluster_ca.description: Whether the served chain verifies against the cluster CA bundle.

provider_id.description: spec.providerID, which names the machine at its cloud provider.

istio_mtls_mode.description: The Istio peer-authentication mode in force for the namespace (namespace policy, else mesh policy, else permissive); not_meshed without Istio.

tls_secrets_readable.description: Present only when reading TLS Secrets is enabled: whether this namespace's could be listed.

workload.description: A controller and what its pod template declares: images and ports, nothing else of the pod spec (no environment, no commands, no arguments).

kind.description: Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, CronJob, Job, ReplicaSet, Pod (a pod nothing owns), Node (a static pod), or the kind of another controller that owns the pods.

secret_volumes.description: Names of the Secrets the pod template mounts as volumes. Names only.

mtls_mode.description: The mesh mTLS mode in force for this workload's pods.

pod.description: A pod that has an address. Evidence for its workload, not an object of its own.

host_network.description: true: the addresses are the node's own.

backing.description: What answers behind the Service. `workloads` is non-empty exactly when this is `workloads`.

target_port.description: As declared: a number or a container port name.

resolved_target_ports.description: The numbers the endpoints actually use for this port.

tls.description: Whether a tls entry covers this host.

key_request.description: What spec.privateKey asks cert-manager to generate. Settings only.

cert_manager_issuer.description: An Issuer or ClusterIssuer of cert-manager.io. An issuer of another group is known only through the issuer_ref of the Certificates that name it.

tls_secret.description: A Secret of type kubernetes.io/tls, sent only when the cluster's administrators enabled reading them. The certificates of its tls.crt and ca.crt entries, and nothing of any other entry: there is no field for one.

certificate_chain.description: The certificates of the tls.crt entry, leaf first.

ca_certificates.description: The certificates of the ca.crt entry.

unparsed_entries.description: Certificate entries that did not parse.

certificate_chain.description: The chain as served, leaf first.

chains_to_cluster_ca.description: Whether the served chain verifies against the cluster CA bundle.

ca_bundle.description: The certificates of clientConfig.caBundle. Empty: the API server's own trust roots are used.

traefik_ref.description: A TLSOption or TLSStore by name. namespace is the route's when the route did not name one. provider is set when the name used Traefik's cross-provider form (name@provider); namespace is then absent, and the object is not one of this cluster's API objects.

traefik_ingress_route.description: A Traefik IngressRoute or IngressRouteTCP as the cluster's API declares it. Declared, not scanned. TLS set in Traefik's static or file configuration is not visible here.

api_group.description: The API group the object was read from. The same namespace and name can exist in both groups; they are two objects.

match.description: The rule, redacted: matcher names, operators and grouping are kept; the quoted arguments of Host, HostSNI, HostRegexp, HostSNIRegexp, Path, PathPrefix, PathRegexp, Method and ALPN are kept; of Header, HeaderRegexp, Headers, HeadersRegexp, Query and QueryRegexp only the first argument (the key name); every other literal is [REDACTED]. Redacted, then cut to 1024 characters. Absent when the rule could not be tokenised safely.

hosts.description: The host names of Host(...) or HostSNI(...) in the rule, lower case, sorted, only where certain: none for a rule with a negation or a host regular expression, an || inside parentheses, or a top-level alternative that names no host.

port.description: A port number or name, as written; left out when it is neither.

tls.description: Present when the route has a tls block (an empty block is TLS with the default certificate). Secret names only: no Secret is read.

effective_options.description: The TLSOption in force, resolved by the agent: the referenced one; else the one TLSOption named default (any namespace); else Traefik's built-in options, also when more than one is named default (default_conflict). Absent on a passthrough route (TLS is not terminated) and when the TLSOptions could not be read and the route references none. What referenced means is that the route names this option, not that Traefik serves it: Traefik registers any TLSOption named default as the global default, so a reference to a TLSOption named default in a namespace may not resolve as written; and Traefik refuses a cross-namespace options or store reference unless allowCrossNamespace is set in its static configuration, which the agent cannot see. default_conflict counts TLSOptions named default from both API groups; Traefik v3 no longer reads traefik.containo.us, so a stale legacy default can set it on a v3 cluster.

traefik_tls_option.description: A Traefik TLSOption. Only what the object declares; a setting it leaves out has Traefik's default.

api_group.description: The API group the object was read from. The same namespace and name can exist in both groups; they are two objects.

secret_names.description: The Secrets that hold the CA certificates, by name; they are not read.

traefik_tls_store.description: A Traefik TLSStore: the names of the Secrets it serves, never their content.

api_group.description: The API group the object was read from. The same namespace and name can exist in both groups; they are two objects.
